sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed challenging order dated 15.03.2019 passed by the Collector, Anuppur in Case No.1529/10/Land Acquisition/2019 directing the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) Kotma,
District-Anuppur to not to disburse the amount of compensation consequent to land acquisition under the provisions of the Coal Bearing Areas Act, 1957.
It is directed that disbursal of compensation be stopped under the intimation to the office of the Collector.

2. On the directions of this Court dated 01.09.2023, Collector Anuppur Shri Ashish Vashishth son of Shri Mukesh Kumar Sharma has filed an affidavit in paragraph-10 of which it is mentioned as under :
"The deponent respectfully submit that the Collector is not empowered under the law to pass such order dated 15.03.2019 under C.B. Act, 1957 and the order dated 15.03.2019 is for only till decision of the complainant.

The petitioner has wrongly interpreted the order of the deponent without disclosing that fact that the SECL has already referred the matter to the Tribunal as there is dispute of the title between the parties."
3. Thereafter, it is mentioned in paragraph-11 as under :
"11.

That, by issuing the letter no.556/SDO/WP/2023 dated 04.09.2023 Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue) Sub Division Kotma, endorsed to General Manage SECL Hasdev area by giving the reference the letter dated 02.09.2023 and in respect of taking the necessary action by order dated 15.03.2019 passed by the Collector.
Copy of the letter dated 04.09.2023 is annexed herewith as Annexure D/5."
4. Thus, it is evident that on the one hand the Collector, Anuppur has admitted that Collector is not empowered under the law to pass such orders like order dated 15.03.2019 under the C.B. Act 1957.
Once this admission has come then the order is a nullity.
It is a void order.
It is an order which is void ab-initio.
Therefore, thereafter the Collector is trying to save his skin by saying that petitioner has wrongly interpreted the order of deponent without disclosing the fact.
That submission is irrelevant.
Once the Collector admits that he has no authority to pass orders as contained in Annexure P/1, then that's end of the matter.
Thereafter, all the actions taken by the Collector pursuant to or in furtherance of will be a nullity.
Therefore, the impugned order Annexure P/1 is hereby quashed.
Parties are relegated to avail the remedies as may be available to them under the law.

5. State for passing an order without authority in an illegal and arbitrary manner will bear the cost of this litigation, which will be payable by the Collector, Anuppur and which is quantified at Rs.25,000/- within a period of 30 days' from the date receipt of certified copy of this order.

The State will be free to recover it from previous Collector, who had pass the impugned order without appreciating the fact and law and also without understanding his own capacity to pass such order as has been admitted by the present Collector.
